turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I’m okay, Doctor. A bit tired, but manageable.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe a 4? It’s a dull ache where they made the cuts.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Sometimes the anesthesia can cause that.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: A little queasy, but not throwing up. I didn’t eat anything yet anyway.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Are you having any trouble breathing or feeling short of breath?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, breathing’s fine. Just a bit of sore throat from the tube, I think.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Do you remember anything from the operating room, or was everything fuzzy?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I don’t remember anything. One minute I was talking, next I was waking up here.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Given your blood pressure and weight, any chest pain or unusual symptoms?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No chest pain. My BP’s been okay, right? I’ve been taking my meds regularly.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: All looks stable. We’ll keep monitoring, but you’re doing well. Rest now, and we’ll get you mobilizing soon.
